title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued its response to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards, outlining plans to improve oversight and ensure AI aligns with public values. It emphasizes commitments to transparency, accountability, and collaboration with industry and academia to establish robust standards for AI deployment and governance.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining its plan to oversee how artificial intelligence is used in the UK's qualifications system, aiming to keep exams fair, reliable and secure. The guidance will set rules and checks so that AI tools don’t compromise assessment quality or student trust.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected works are used when training AI systems, evaluating the legal and ethical implications. It offers recommendations to balance creators' rights with the benefits of AI development.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government responds to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, outlining its commitments to support innovation, strengthen regulation, and address safety concerns. It stresses the need for balanced policies that foster growth while protecting citizens and maintaining the UK’s global competitiveness in AI.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope, objectives, and guidelines for a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence intersects with public standards. It includes a clear set of terms of reference and frequently asked questions to help members understand the committee’s role and responsibilities.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee in response to an inquiry about the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission likely outlines CSPL’s perspectives, concerns, or recommendations regarding AI oversight and policy frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy examines how artificial intelligence will change rules for medical products, ensuring safety and effectiveness as AI technologies grow. It uses the principles from the AI White Paper to guide new regulatory standards and best practices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make our organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential user of AI among similarly sized defence forces worldwide. It focuses on leveraging AI to strengthen operational capabilities and maintain global leadership in defence technology.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to take advantage of AI’s benefits while carefully managing its risks. It focuses on partnership, risk mitigation and unlocking AI opportunities across the industry.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report reviews how copyright-protected works are used in developing AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It highlights progress made, identifies challenges, and suggests future steps to balance creators’ rights with AI innovation.
